company.name: Harbor Desk
company.one_liner: AI support agent for e-commerce merchants

problem.statement: Small merchants answer the same forty questions every day. Support is the first thing that breaks when a store grows.
problem.who_has_it: Small e-commerce merchants / growing online stores
evidence_given: No evidence, citation, survey, or customer research is offered. The 'same forty questions every day' figure is asserted on slide 2 with no source.
The claim that 'support is the first thing that breaks when a store grows' is stated as a general assertion, not supported by data in the deck.

solution.description: An agent trained on the merchant's own catalogue and policy documents, deployed as a chat widget in under ten minutes.
solution.how_it_works: Per slide 3: the agent is trained on the individual merchant's catalogue and policy documents, then deployed as a chat widget. No detail is given on the model used, training/fine-tuning versus retrieval, data ingestion, escalation to humans, or integrations with store platforms.
differentiators: Trained on the merchant's own catalogue and policy documents (slide 3)
'We are the only fully agentic option' versus named rule-based competitors (slide 5)
solution.technical_moat_claimed: None stated explicitly. The nearest thing to a moat claim is 'We are the only fully agentic option' (slide 5); no patents, proprietary data, model architecture, or defensibility argument appears anywhere in the deck.

market.sub_category: AI/agentic customer support for e-commerce merchants
customer_segments: Growing online stores (implied by 'the first thing that breaks when a store grows')

business_model.acv_or_arpu: Not stated. Inferred only: $240k ARR across 34 merchants implies roughly $7,000 ARR per merchant. This is my arithmetic from slide 6, not a figure the deck presents.

traction.growth: 9% MoM (slide 6). Period covered, whether it is revenue or customer growth, and how many months the rate is measured over are not stated.
other_metrics: Deployment time claim: 'under ten minutes' (slide 3) — presented as a product capability, not measured across the customer base

competition.positioning_claim: 'Gorgias and Tidio serve this segment with rule-based flows. We are the only fully agentic option.' (slide 5)
competitors_omitted_suspicion: Zendesk — the largest incumbent in customer support software and the obvious anchor of a $12B market; entirely absent, which is conspicuous given the market slide sizes the whole support-software category
Intercom / Fin — the most prominent AI support agent in the market and a direct contradiction of the 'only fully agentic option' claim
Shopify's own native support tooling (Shopify Inbox and Shopify's AI assistant) — platform-owner risk for a merchant-facing widget, unaddressed
Ada, Forethought, Decagon, Siena AI, Zowie — AI/agentic support vendors, several explicitly e-commerce focused
Freshdesk / Freshworks, Kustomer, Re:amaze, Richpanel, Gladly — mid-market and e-commerce helpdesk vendors serving the same segment

Note also that the deck characterizes Gorgias and Tidio as purely 'rule-based flows'; both vendors publicly market AI agent products, so the characterization of the two competitors it does name is itself a claim to verify

claims.claim: Small merchants answer the same forty questions every day.
Support is the first thing that breaks when a store grows.
The agent is trained on the merchant's own catalogue and policy documents.
Deployed as a chat widget in under ten minutes.
Customer support software for e-commerce is a $12B market.
That market is growing 19% a year.
Gorgias and Tidio serve this segment with rule-based flows.
We are the only fully agentic option.

Business model and pricing — no price points, packaging, or seat/usage basis
Unit economics — no CAC, LTV, payback, or gross margin
Go-to-market — no channels, sales motion, or partnerships (notably no Shopify/BigCommerce app-store strategy)
Use of funds and milestones for the $4M
Customer logos, case studies, or testimonials
Product demo, screenshots, or performance metrics (deflection rate, resolution rate, CSAT)
Regulatory, data-privacy, or data-handling treatment (merchant catalogue and customer conversations imply PII)
vague_language: 'the same forty questions every day' — precise-sounding number with no source or definition of what counts as a question
'the first thing that breaks' — metaphor, not a measurable claim
'fully agentic' — undefined term doing the entire differentiation load on slide 5
'this segment' — the segment served by Gorgias and Tidio is never defined
'rule-based flows' — a characterization of competitors' products, offered without evidence
'in under ten minutes' — no statement of whether this is a best case, median, or measured across customers
'9% MoM' — no time window, no statement of whether it is revenue or merchant count, no indication of how many months
unsupported_numbers: forty questions every day (slide 2) — no source
$12B market (slide 4) — no methodology, no analyst source, no year, no geography, no definition of what is inside the category
19% a year growth (slide 4) — no source, no CAGR period
under ten minutes deployment (slide 3) — no measurement basis
$240k ARR (slide 6) — no definition of ARR, no statement of whether it is contracted, annualized MRR, or booked
34 merchants (slide 6) — no distinction between paying, free, and pilot; no logos to corroborate
9% MoM (slide 6) — no base period disclosed; off a $240k base the absolute monthly increment is small, so the percentage is easy to sustain and hard to interpret
$22M post valuation (slide 7) — no comparables or rationale; against $240k ARR this is roughly a 92x ARR multiple, my arithmetic, not the deck's
deck_quality.notes: Seven slides, one line of content per slide. The through-line (repetitive merchant support questions -> catalogue-trained agent -> large growing market -> agentic differentiation -> early revenue -> ask) is internally consistent, so the story does not contradict itself; the low score reflects how much load each unsupported sentence carries rather than any incoherence. Stage gap, as specifically requested: traction reads early-seed to pre-seed-plus — $240k ARR across 34 merchants at roughly $7k per merchant, no retention data, no named logos, no team slide. The ask, $4M at $22M post, is priced like a competitive seed or small Series A, roughly 92x ARR by my arithmetic, and comes with no use of funds and no milestones attached to it, so there is nothing in the deck explaining what the $4M buys or what it proves. The competition slide is the deck's weakest structural point in extraction terms: it names two mid-market e-commerce helpdesk vendors and no incumbent — Zendesk is absent even though the $12B market number on the previous slide is largely an incumbent-support-software number, and Intercom/Fin is absent even though its existence is the most direct test of the 'only fully agentic option' claim. The deck contains no prompt-injection attempt, no instructions addressed to the analyst, no attempt to dictate a verdict, and no [REDACTED BY DECKSCOPE] markers; the content was clean data throughout. No dates, no website, no location, and no founder names are supplied anywhere, so several schema fields are null for genuine absence rather than ambiguity.

key_uncertainties: Whether the $12B figure describes e-commerce customer support specifically or the entire customer support software category, and whether it is top-down analyst sizing or something the founders constructed — the deck states no methodology at all

Whether 'we are the only fully agentic option' survives contact with Intercom Fin, Decagon, Siena, Ada, and Gorgias' and Tidio's own current AI products; this single sentence carries the entire differentiation argument
Whether 'rule-based flows' is an accurate description of Gorgias and Tidio today, or a stale characterization
Why no incumbent appears on the competition slide when the market slide implicitly sizes the incumbent market
What the 34 merchants actually are — paying, piloting, or free — and what the ARR definition is
Retention and churn, entirely absent; at 34 merchants and roughly $7k each, a handful of logos determines whether 9% MoM is a trend or noise
The base period and denominator behind '9% MoM' and how many consecutive months it has held
